xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4740: Linked machine over Fly proxy: first request after idle fails with 'socket hang up'

plan.title: Linked machine over Fly proxy: first request after idle fails with 'socket hang up'
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: LinkAgent (src/lib/anywhere/link-client.ts) pools secure channels with keepAlive but no `timeout`, so Node's keepSocketAlive ignores the peer's `Keep-Alive: timeout=5` hint and a free channel never expires. The linked machine's stock HTTP server closes idle channels after 5 s; behind the Fly WebSocket proxy home does not see that close before its next request, reuses the dead channel, and the request fails with `socket hang up` (ECONNRESET, req.reusedSocket true). ChannelSocket's idle timer is also one-shot, unlike net.Socket, so a channel whose timer fired once mid-request never expires in the pool afterwards.
narratives.Proposal: Two layers. (1) Give LinkAgent an explicit pool idle timeout LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS = 4000 (below the 5 s server keep-alive; Node lowers it further for a shorter hint) and make ChannelSocket's idle timer re-arm on traffic like net.Socket. (2) In linkFetch and linkForward, when a GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request dies with ECONNRESET or EPIPE on a reused pooled channel before any response byte, close the pool's other idle channels and resend it exactly once on a fresh channel. Non-safe methods are never resent. Document both in docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md and the link-client.ts header.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Raising or changing the linked machine's HTTP server keepAliveTimeout
- WebSocket-level pings on the /ws/link transport
- Resending POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or any other non-safe method
- Resending more than once
- Making LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS configurable or adding any config key
- Changing channel-agent.ts, openLinkSocket, ws-linked.ts or port-forwards.ts (they open their own channels and are not pooled through LinkAgent)
- Retrying a failure on a freshly opened channel, after a response began, on abort, on a linkForward timeout, or on a LinkUnavailableError
- A live reproduction against a real Fly machine as an acceptance gate

autoDecisions.summary: Fix both layers: pool idle expiry and a one-time resend on a stale reused channel.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue lists both as candidate fixes; expiry removes the common idle case and the resend covers a channel that dies inside the expiry window (proxy or VM restart). Neither alone covers every path.

autoDecisions.summary: LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS = 4000, passed as the http.Agent `timeout` option; not configurable.
autoDecisions.rationale: It sits below the linked machine's 5 s keepAliveTimeout and equals what Node derives from the `timeout=5` hint (5000 minus the 1000 ms agentKeepAliveTimeoutBuffer). Passing it as the agent option lets Node's own keepSocketAlive apply it and lower it for a shorter hint.

autoDecisions.summary: Resend only safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS).
autoDecisions.rationale: A resent POST could start a second agent or deliver a conversation message twice. After the 4 s expiry a POST reaches a stale channel only inside a narrow window and then fails loudly as it does today, which the caller can handle. The issue's observed failures were GETs (conversation-list fetch).

autoDecisions.summary: Exactly one resend, after destroying the agent's other free channels.
autoDecisions.rationale: With maxSockets 4, channels idle together and die together; a bare resend could land on a sibling stale channel. agent.freeSockets is a public Node property.

autoDecisions.summary: Fix ChannelSocket's one-shot idle timer in channel-socket.ts instead of overriding keepSocketAlive in LinkAgent.
autoDecisions.rationale: Its header already promises net.Socket semantics; a planning probe showed net.Socket fires twice when traffic follows the first timeout while ChannelSocket fires once. Fixing the socket keeps pool expiry working after a mid-request timeout for every consumer.

autoDecisions.summary: No live Fly reproduction is required; unit tests reproduce the mechanism.
autoDecisions.rationale: Planning probes reproduced every step (free socket timeout 0 without an agent timeout, 4000 with it; reused-socket hang-up yields ECONNRESET 'socket hang up' with reusedSocket true) on loopback; a Fly check costs money and is not deterministic.

metadata.sizeJustification: Small bug fix: 2 source files, 2 test files, 1 doc file in one subsystem (src/lib/anywhere).

items.title: Give LinkAgent a 4 s pool idle timeout (LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS)

expected_outputs: link-client.test.ts passes including the three new 'pooled channels (PAN-4740)' tests

narrative.Action: Follow PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4740.md WI-1. In src/lib/anywhere/link-client.ts add `export const LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS = 4_000;` (with the doc comment from the PRD) below LINK_WAIT_MS, and change the LinkAgent constructor's `super({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 4, ...options })` to `super({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 4, timeout: LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS, ...options })`. Add a `describe('pooled channels (PAN-4740)')` block to src/lib/anywhere/__tests__/link-client.test.ts using a real loopback node:http server and a LinkAgent whose createConnection is overridden to net.connect(port) (call back on 'connect', return undefined) and counted. The existing duplexPair stand-in cannot be pooled because keepSocketAlive calls setKeepAlive on it. Pass agent and routeSource through linkFetch init. After each request await setImmediate, then read Object.values(agent.freeSockets).flat(). No timer waits in these tests: emit 'timeout' directly.
narrative.Why: Without an agent timeout Node's keepSocketAlive ignores the peer's Keep-Alive hint and a pooled channel never expires, so home reuses channels the linked machine closed after 5 s.

items.title: Given a loopback server with keepAliveTimeout 60000, when one linkFetch GET completes through a LinkAgent, then the single free socket's `.timeout` equals LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS (4000)
Given a loopback server with keepAliveTimeout 3000 (hint timeout=3), when one linkFetch GET completes, then the free socket's `.timeout` equals 2000

Given one completed GET leaves a free socket, when the test emits 'timeout' on it, then the socket is destroyed and the next linkFetch GET returns 200 over a second connection (createConnection counter equals 2)
The existing test that constructs LinkAgent with { keepAlive: false } still passes unchanged, because the options argument still overrides the defaults
Re-arm ChannelSocket's idle timer on traffic after it fires (net.Socket semantics)

expected_outputs: channel.test.ts passes including the two new 'ChannelSocket idle timeout (PAN-4740)' tests

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-2 exactly. In src/lib/anywhere/channel/channel-socket.ts extract a private armIdle() that creates the unref'd timer (whose callback sets idleTimer = null and emits 'timeout'); setTimeout(ms) calls clearIdle(), stores idleMs, registers the optional callback, then calls armIdle() when idleMs > 0; touch() refreshes a live timer, or calls armIdle() when idleTimer is null, idleMs > 0 and the socket is not destroyed. clearIdle() is unchanged. In src/lib/anywhere/channel/__tests__/channel.test.ts add describe('ChannelSocket idle timeout (PAN-4740)') that builds a ChannelSocket over one side of duplexPair() with the dummy handshake from the PRD (tx/rx/localPublicKey/remotePublicKey 32-byte fills, hash 64-byte fill; this construction was verified in a planning probe), calls vi.useFakeTimers() after construction, and destroys the channel at the end.
narrative.Why: A reused pooled channel keeps the 4 s pool timer while it serves a request; if that timer fires mid-request, the one-shot timer never re-arms, keepSocketAlive sees socket.timeout already equal to the agent timeout and does not reset it, and the channel never expires in the pool.

items.title: Given a ChannelSocket with setTimeout(1000) under fake timers, when 1000 ms pass, then it emits 'timeout' once; when channel.write(Buffer.from('x')) follows and another 1000 ms pass, then it has emitted 'timeout' twice
Given a ChannelSocket whose timeout fired once, when setTimeout(0) is called, a write follows and 5000 ms pass, then no further 'timeout' is emitted (count stays 1)
When channel.test.ts runs after the change, then the existing tests (Noise IK open, WebSocket upgrade close(4401), handshake timeout under fake timers) still pass without edits
Resend a GET/HEAD/OPTIONS once when a reused pooled channel hangs up before any response

expected_outputs: link-client.test.ts passes including the five new resend tests

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-3 exactly. In src/lib/anywhere/link-client.ts add RETRY_SAFE_METHODS (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS), STALE_CHANNEL_CODES (ECONNRESET, EPIPE), the exported pure isStaleChannelFailure(method, error, { reusedSocket, responded }), and a private dropIdleChannels(agent) that destroys every socket in agent.freeSockets. Wrap the request bodies of linkFetch and linkForward in a local attempt() function that tracks `responded` (set at the top of the response callback) and attaches { reusedSocket: req.reusedSocket === true, responded } to a rejected error under a module-level symbol. Call attempt(); on rejection, rethrow unless the facts are present, init.signal is not aborted and isStaleChannelFailure is true; otherwise dropIdleChannels(agent) and return attempt() once more. linkForward's 'timeout' handler and size cap live inside attempt(). Update the link-client.ts header comment to state the pool idle expiry and the one-resend rule. Add the five tests named in PRD WI-3 to link-client.test.ts using the loopback harness from pool-idle-expiry, with a server that destroys the socket of a chosen request number without answering.
narrative.Why: Expiry cannot cover a channel that dies inside the 4 s window (proxy or VM restart). Node documents a reused socket that hangs up before any response as the server-closed-idle-connection case; resending a safe request once fixes it without duplicate side effects.

items.title: Given a server that answers request 1, destroys request 2 and answers request 3, when a second linkFetch GET runs on the reused channel, then it resolves with status 200, the server saw 3 requests and createConnection ran 2 times
Given the same server, when the second call is linkFetch with method POST, then it rejects with code ECONNRESET and the server saw exactly 2 requests (no resend)
Given a server that destroys request 1, when the first linkFetch GET runs on a fresh channel, then it rejects with code ECONNRESET and the server saw exactly 1 request
Given the request-2-destroying server, when linkForward({ method: 'GET', path: '/x' }) runs on the reused channel, then it resolves with status 200 from a second connection

isStaleChannelFailure returns true for ('GET', ECONNRESET, reused, no response) and ('head', EPIPE, reused, no response), and returns false for POST, for reusedSocket false, for responded true, and for code ETIMEDOUT
Document pool idle expiry and the one-resend rule in ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md

expected_outputs: each grep prints exactly one matching line inside the 'One session per connection; the same port' section

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-4. In docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md, section 'One session per connection; the same port (D-4645-3, D-4645-4)', after the sentence ending '…which is exactly what the first smoke run hit.' add the paragraph given verbatim in the PRD: pooled channels close after LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS (4 s) or sooner on a shorter Keep-Alive hint; why (5 s server keep-alive, Fly proxy may hide the close, PAN-4740); GET/HEAD/OPTIONS that die on a reused channel before any response with ECONNRESET or EPIPE are resent once after closing the pool's other idle channels; other methods are never resent; ChannelSocket.setTimeout re-arms on traffic like net.Socket. configuration/linked-machines.mdx is not changed: it documents no pooling or retry behavior.
narrative.Why: The architecture doc is the developer reference for LinkAgent pooling; it must describe the new expiry and resend behavior.

items.title: Given the doc change, when a reader opens the 'One session per connection' section of docs/ANYWHERE-ARCHITECTURE.md, then it shows LINK_POOL_IDLE_MS with its 4 s value and says a shorter Keep-Alive hint from the other machine closes the channel sooner

Given the doc change, when a reader opens the same section, then it states that GET, HEAD and OPTIONS requests that die with ECONNRESET or EPIPE on a reused channel are resent once, and that other methods are never resent
